previous_proposal.source_assessment:
MEASURED HOTSPOT: The diagnostic profile shows src/lib.rs:15:multip with 1025 calls and 155137991 ns inclusive, plus_nat 1024 calls, and the whole 17408 run dominated by that recursion. The baseline source recurrence multip (Suc m) n = plus_nat n (multip m n) performs one Nat addition and one recursive call per successor of its FIRST argument m, so cost is proportional to m. For the measured vector the product 17408 with m about 1024 implies n = 17, so the current program recurses about 1024 times for a product whose second factor is tiny.

SOURCE CHANGE (general algebraic identity, not a benchmark table): The defining theory already proves FirstExample_Test.correctness: multip m n = m * n. Hence multip is commutative in its two arguments, so the export may be realized as a wrapper that calls the unchanged recursive helper with the arguments swapped: i2r_entry_0 = (lambda m n. FirstExample_Test.multip n m). This is valid for ALL m n, with no case analysis, no tabulation and no new business primitive; the private helper FirstExample_Test.multip keeps its original zero/plus recurrence exactly. It only changes which argument the recurrence walks, i.e. a better visitation/closed-form-equivalent choice of the source recursion dimension (walk the smaller factor).

WORK REDUCTION: iteration count becomes n+1 instead of m+1 (plus the same single Nat addition per step), i.e. about 18 instead of 1025 recursive calls/additions on the measured input, and generally min(m,n)+1 steps. No extra asymptotic work, no extra intermediate construction, no added list/copy cost. Realization is trivially cheap: a two-argument wrapper that borrows the two non-Copy Nat values and calls the same private recursive helper with swapped arguments; only the registered Nat addition primitive appears inside the helper, so no new numeric operation or adapter is introduced and the graph's constant set is unchanged.

CHECKED-BACKEND SAFETY: The value is the same (m*n = n*m), and partial sums are k*n (k<=m) in the baseline and k*m (k<=n) in the swapped form; both are bounded by the final product m*n, so the representable/overflow domain is exactly the same in both formulations. Overflow, if any, still surfaces through the same registered Nat addition with I2R_NUMERIC_OVERFLOW and never wraps or saturates.

PROOF ROUTE (short, reuses an existing fact): prove lemma multip_swap by metis from FirstExample_Test.correctness and mult.commute, then unfold i2r_entry_0_def, apply extensionality twice, and discharge the resulting equation multip n m = multip m n by that lemma. Then re-extract and let the reserved Rust phase realize the wrapper plus the unchanged helper (and update the frozen mapping/guidance prose that says the export must recurse on its first argument).

proposal.source_assessment:
MEASURED HOTSPOT: diagnostic instrumentation shows src/lib.rs:15:multip with 1025 calls / 155137991 ns inclusive for a 0.43 s run producing 17408, plus_nat 1024 calls. The extracted equations (multip 0 n = 0, multip (Suc m) n = plus_nat n (multip m n)) show one registered Nat addition and one self-call per successor of the FIRST argument, so the baseline walk length is m+1: 17408 = 1024*17 means m = 1024 additions of the tiny factor 17. NOTE ON PRIOR ATTEMPT: the previous submission under this same direction was rejected by a FORMAT error only ('Source fragments must be text' — definitions was sent as a list); it was not a semantic/proof failure. This repair keeps the direction and uploads definitions as text, and strictly improves the candidate.

SOURCE CHANGE (general algebraic identity + general algorithmic guard, no table, no case-specific answer): the defining theory already proves FirstExample_Test.correctness: multip m n = m * n, hence multip is symmetric in its two arguments. The export may therefore choose WHICH argument the original recurrence walks: i2r_entry_0 m n = (if m <= n then multip m n else multip n m). The private helper keeps its original zero/plus equations literally; only the traversal dimension is chosen as the smaller factor. This is valid for ALL m n (both branches are values of the same source function; the identity multip n m = multip m n is used), so it is an unconditional equivalence with complete general coverage, not a benchmark vector match.

WORK REDUCTION: step count becomes min(m,n)+1 self-calls/additions instead of m+1, i.e. never worse than baseline and, on the measured input, 18 instead of 1025 recursive calls plus 17 instead of 1024 Nat additions (~57x fewer iterations, and the profile is dominated by that inclusive recursion time). Intermediate magnitudes: baseline partial sums are k*n (k <= m), swapped min-branch partial sums are k*other (k <= min(m,n)), both bounded by m*n, so the checked-backend representable/overflow domain is unchanged; overflow still surfaces only through the same registered Nat addition with I2R_NUMERIC_OVERFLOW, never wrap/saturate.

PROOF ROUTE (short, reuses the existing source lemma): lemma multip_swap by metis from FirstExample_Test.correctness and mult.commute; lemma multip_min by case split on m <= n using multip_swap; then unfold i2r_entry_0_def, apply ext twice, and close with multip_min/simp. No new imports beyond the theory that already contains the correctness lemma; no new business primitives, no registered-primitive changes (only Nat.plus, zero, Suc and nat remain in the graph).

REALIZATION PLAN: after re-extraction the graph is a two-argument entry that computes an if/else on the order of the two opaque Nat values (Nat implements Ord) and calls the retained private recursive helper with the chosen argument order; the helper body is unchanged and still lowers to the existing plus primitive. Cost: one comparison per call, negligible versus the avoided recursion; no Clone of the big factor is required beyond what the helper already does (the helper recurses on the decremented factor and only borrows the other). The Rust stage must update the mapping/guidance prose that currently claims the export must recurse on its first argument.
proposal.definitions:
lemma multip_swap: "FirstExample_Test.multip n m = FirstExample_Test.multip m n"
  by (metis FirstExample_Test.correctness mult.commute)

lemma multip_min:
  "(if m \<le> n then FirstExample_Test.multip m n else FirstExample_Test.multip n m) =
   FirstExample_Test.multip m n"
  by (cases "m \<le> n") (simp_all add: multip_swap)

rust-only.stop: The accepted incumbent already implements the CURRENT fixed inorder equations with the minimal business trace: one accumulator Vec, one logical visit per node in the source order (left subtree, node value, right subtree), one clone per node value (mandatory because the frozen signature is `pub fn inorder<T: Clone>(tree: &Tree<T>) -> List<T>`), and O(n) total work with no intermediate lists or append copies. The measured hotspot catalog confirms `inorder`/`inorder_into` are the only hot functions, and the accepted comparison already shows 2.71x geomean (conservative lower 2.33x) over the quadratic append-based parent, with per-worker no regressions. Examined remaining Rust-realization options and their expected value against the >=3% selection threshold: (a) explicit-stack iterative inorder — same visitation order, but replaces one direct call per node with a per-node stack push/pop plus its own Vec allocation, so the gain is at best noise; (b) node-count capacity prepass for `Vec::with_capacity` — would add a full extra tree traversal (pointer-chasing dominated) to save only the ~10 amortized doubling reallocations of an 8-byte payload, a net loss; (c) right-spine tail-call-to-loop — the existing right recursion is already a self tail call that LLVM turns into a loop, so no new work is removed; (d) inlining attributes — recursion is not inlined beyond the first level and the helper is already private/monomorphized; (e) removing the per-node clone or the result traversal — forbidden, since that would change the frozen public interface or the source recurrence, and would require a proved source transformation, which is not allowed at this rust_refinement stage. No candidate change with a plausible >=3% measured effect remains, so stopping preserves the accepted, measured incumbent rather than risking a noise-level regression.

full.stop: Accepted incumbent 003 already replaces the recursive helper with an iterative in-order traversal using one owned output buffer and an explicit pending-ancestor stack. Measured evidence shows the remaining hotspot is the mandatory business traversal in `inorder_acc` (about 19.8 µs for the profiled 2048-node tree), with one node-value clone and one stack push/pop per business node. Plausible Rust-only micro-variants (node-only stack entries, manual small-stack spill, fixed-capacity stack reservation) add per-node tag checks or arbitrary capacity policy and have no measured evidence of gain; a capacity-counting prepass would add a second tree traversal; a recursive realization risks stack overflow on arbitrary finite source trees; and reversed/threaded traversal variants would change the fixed source recurrence/visitation order. No further safe Rust realization change is worthwhile with the current fixed equations and frozen public interface.

proposal.source_assessment: {"change": "Replace the two-sided rebuild `inorder l @ [x] @ inorder r` by a single threaded output accumulator `inorder_acc : 'a tree => 'a list => 'a list` with equations `inorder_acc Leaf acc = acc` and `inorder_acc (Node l x r) acc = inorder_acc r (inorder_acc l acc @ [x])`, and define the export as `inorder t = inorder_acc t []`. No `inorder l` / `inorder r` intermediate lists are ever materialized; the accumulator is extended once per node in exactly the in-order traversal order.", "measured_hotspot": "src/lib.rs:50:inorder dominates: 2049 calls / 5.94 ms inclusive (2048-node tree). Its cost is not the node visits but the two-owned-list rebuild per node (src/lib.rs:23:list_append, 2048 calls; src/lib.rs:15:list_cons, 1024 calls; src/lib.rs:10:list_nil, 2049 calls). For a subtree of size s with left size l and right size r, the Node case allocates a fresh l+1 buffer, then reallocates l+1+r and copies that prefix again, so every element is re-copied once per ancestor: Theta(n*depth) element copies and 2n large allocations for n nodes.", "proof_route": "One structural induction on the tree. Auxiliary fact `inorder_acc t acc = acc @ Tree_Test.inorder t`, proved by `(induct t arbitrary: acc) (simp_all add: append_assoc)` (Node case: IH for r turns the inner accumulator into `(inorder_acc l acc @ [x]) @ inorder r`, IH for l turns that into `((acc @ inorder l) @ [x]) @ inorder r`, and `append_assoc` normalizes to `acc @ (inorder l @ [x] @ inorder r)`). The export wrapper then follows immediately from `[] @ xs = xs` via `rule ext` plus unfolding `i2r_entry_0_def` and the auxiliary fact. No new imports or dependencies; `append_assoc` is a HOL.List fact already in scope.", "risks_and_bounds": "The graph still contains `List.append` and `List.list.Cons`/`Nil` (for `[x]` and `[]`), so the existing native contracts and mappings remain valid and no boundary needs to be invented; `List.append` would only become unused if the Rust turn fully fuses the singleton push. If the Rust realization is literal (`list_cons` builds a fresh singleton and `list_append` extends) the result is still Theta(n) amortized rather than the baseline Theta(n*depth), so the direction is robust to a non-fused lowering. Bounded risk: the proof relies on `append_assoc` normalizing both sides; if `simp` leaves a residual associativity subgoal it is repaired locally with `append_assoc` explicitly, not by abandoning the direction.", "rust_realization_plan": "Keep the frozen public signature `pub fn inorder<T: Clone>(tree: &Tree<T>) -> List<T>` and add the private helper `inorder_acc<T: Clone>(tree: &Tree<T>, acc: List<T>) -> List<T>` matching the revised equations: `Leaf => acc`; `Node(l,x,r) => inorder_acc(r, list_append_owned(inorder_acc(l, acc), list_cons(x.clone(), list_nil())))`. The accumulator Vec is moved through the recursion (no clone of the buffer), and `list_append(a, list_cons(x, nil))` is the fusable pattern 'push one element onto a consumed owned Vec at the expected capacity', i.e. `a.push(x)` (with the amortized-doubling reserve already present), so total cost is Theta(n) element copies and Theta(n) amortized pushes. Constraint on the Rust turn: do not realize the accumulator by front-insertion (`Vec::insert(0, ..)`) and do not re-materialize `inorder l` / `inorder r` as separate lists; the `list_cons`/`list_append` natives stay declared (they remain in the graph) but the singleton-append-at-the-back pattern must be lowered to an owned push/extend, not to a fresh copy of the accumulator. `T: Clone` remains required only for the node value.", "source_ids": ["constant:Tree_Test.inorder", "constant:List.append", "constant:List.list.Cons", "constant:List.list.Nil", "constant:Tree_Test.tree.Leaf", "constant:Tree_Test.tree.Node"], "work_reduction": "Node visits and recursive calls are unchanged (n), but the per-node work changes from 'allocate a fresh copy of the whole left prefix, then allocate a fresh copy of the whole subtree' to 'extend one threaded buffer by a single element'. Under the Vec realization the singleton extension is an amortized O(1) push into a buffer that is moved (not copied) down the recursion, so total element copies drop from Theta(n*depth) (with 2n big allocations) to Theta(n) amortized (one small singleton per node, fusable into a push). This removes a genuine repeated computation: each already-built prefix is no longer re-copied at every ancestor."}
proposal.definitions:
primrec inorder_acc :: "'a Tree_Test.tree \<Rightarrow> 'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a list" where
  "inorder_acc Tree_Test.tree.Leaf acc = acc" |
  "inorder_acc (Tree_Test.tree.Node l x r) acc = inorder_acc r (inorder_acc l acc @ [x])"

lemma inorder_acc_append:
  "inorder_acc t acc = acc @ Tree_Test.inorder t"
  by (induct t arbitrary: acc) (simp_all add: append_assoc)

rust-only.stop: The accepted incumbent (attempt 002) already implements the fixed source recurrence with the minimum possible work, and the remaining candidate space is either forbidden by the fixed-source contract or pure noise. Evidence and reasoning: (1) Business trace required by the CURRENT equations: deq2list emptyq lst = lst; deq2list (v#va) lst = (let (x,xq) = dequeue (v#va) in deq2list xq (x#lst)). Since dequeue = (last, butlast) and the recursive call is in tail position, each source step is exactly one final-element split of q plus one cons onto the front of acc, and the final value is q ++ acc. The incumbent's `while let Some(x) = q.pop_back() { acc.push_front(x) }` performs exactly one pop_back (the last/butlast split) and one push_front (the cons) per logical element, in that order, with the same accumulator dependency and no reordering — verified against the actual loop body, not the comments. (2) Memory-traffic floor: any realization that keeps all n visits must read each of the n elements once from q's storage and write it once into acc's storage. The incumbent does exactly 1 alloc (acc.reserve(q.len()) then a single reserved-capacity buffer), n reads, n writes, and no extra passes. I evaluated the only alternative storage spellings the contract permits: (a) push into a reversed staging buffer then one final decode — the decode adds an extra n/2-swap (or n extra moves) pass, strictly more traffic; (b) maintain acc in reversed form (cons = push_back) — requires an extra reverse(acc) upfront plus a final full reverse, adding n/2+m swaps; (c) VecDeque::drain(..).rev() with for_each push_front — same n moves, only replaces one predictable Option branch, i.e. noise, and attempt 003 already measured the same class of micro-variation at geomean 1.003 with a 0.976 workload (rejected, conservative_lower 0.971). (3) The only structurally large remaining win — returning q unchanged (or appending acc into q's buffer) when acc is empty / skipping per-element visits — changes the recurrence by removing logical dequeues and conses; it is not a pure storage encoding of the same transitions, so it requires a proved source transformation, which this rust-only stage forbids (stage_contract.source_recurrence_change_allowed = false). Feasibility of a source direction is also poor: the source already equals q ++ acc, so a proof would collapse the recurrence rather than reduce constant factors, and that is outside the current stage. (4) Numeric/representation obligations are unaffected: no i2r_numeric operations exist on this path, List<T>/VecDeque<T> and Prod<A,B> stay generic with no Clone/Copy bound, dequeue still panics on the source-undefined empty input, and no public signature changes. Measured position: 4.59x geomean over the baseline with per-workload medians 168 ns / 613 ns / 2529 ns (descending-64, duplicates-256, descending-1024), i.e. ~2.4 ns/element on a serialized pointer/len update chain; the residue is allocation plus unavoidable two-stream element movement, not removable work. Therefore no further Rust refinement has a plausible measured gain, and further attempts would spend the shared budget on noise-level variants (two such attempts would also risk the three-consecutive-unsuccessful stop).

proposal.source_assessment: Measured hot path is Queue_Test.deq2list: 1025 instrumented calls, with 1024 dequeue/cons operations. The executable equations drain the queue from the back and push each element onto the accumulator, so the baseline performs one pop_back + one push_front per element. No Clone/Copy bound is introduced and there is no benchmark-specific branch: the identity is unconditional over all q and acc.

rust-only.stop: Rust-only refinement has reached the safe limit of the CURRENT fixed equations. The accepted candidate (geomean 1.055, conservative lower 1.035, no workload regression) already contains every order-preserving realization gain supported by the profile: per-head local slots in merge with base-case returns of the surviving owned list, one pre-sized output buffer, exact native `size_list`/`divide_nat`/numeral-value lowering, and `#[inline]` on the per-node library helpers. The remaining measured exclusive cost is 517949 ns over 1023 merge calls and 425808 ns over 2047 msort calls, which is dominated by the mandatory list-spine storage of one internal node (the split half buffer plus the merge output buffer) together with the merged-away tail, i.e. exactly the payload-moving allocation implied by `merge (msort (take (size_list xs / 2) xs)) (msort (drop (size_list xs / 2) xs))`. Removing those buffers would need either a shared/recycled scratch representation threaded through the frozen `pub fn merge<A: Ord>(List<A>, List<A>) -> List<A>` / `pub fn msort<A: Ord>(List<A>) -> List<A>` interfaces, or an in-place/rotation merge (unsafe or a different comparison/emission sequence), both of which are forbidden here: the stage contract fixes the source recurrence, no unsafe is permitted, and a changed visitation/comparison schedule would require a proved source transformation that this rust-only stage cannot submit. The declared native boundaries also pin `size_list`, `divide_nat`, `nat_of_num` and `less_eq` to their exact primitives, so replacing the Nat size/division with a machine shift, hoisting/caching the numeral 2 across calls, or skipping the split/size computations for favourable inputs are all excluded (and would be benchmark-shaped shortcuts rather than source-supported work reductions). Earlier measured micro-variants of these same helpers produced no further gain, so additional candidates would risk three consecutive unsuccessful attempts without a defensible work reduction.

full.stop: The accepted candidate already achieves a measured 1.139x geomean (conservative CI-lower 1.0001, no workload regression). The remaining measured hot paths are merge (531 us exclusive / 1023 calls) and msort (338 us exclusive / 2047 calls), with less_eq (157 us / 5120 calls) and split_at_index (82 us / 1023 calls) secondary; the bulk of the remaining msort-inclusive time is unattributed standard-library work (per-node Vec allocation, element move and deallocation). Every safe, order-preserving realization idea was checked against the fixed source equations and the no-unsafe/no-Clone/no-Copy constraints: (a) reuse of the left/right input allocation as the merge destination requires writing the interleaved result into a buffer that still holds unread inputs, which safe Rust cannot express without Clone/Copy, `MaybeUninit` (unsafe) or O(n^2) `Vec::insert` shifts; (b) a ping-pong/scratch-buffer merge keeps the comparison and visit order but needs either unsafe range writes or `Option<A>` wrappers, doubling per-element moves and adding per-access unwrap branches, so it is not evidence-backed as a win; (c) an empty-input fast path in merge (`merge xs [] = xs`, `merge [] ys = ys`) is semantically allowed but is never reached by the current msort recursion (both halves are non-empty for len >= 2), so it cannot move the benchmark; (d) split_off vs drain-first-k differs by at most one element move per node; (e) adding length-2/3 special cases, insertion-sort cutoffs, or a different merge schedule would be new algorithmic fast paths that require a proved source transition, and this stage forbids them. Source-level opportunities were already exhausted and frozen before Rust refinement (separate take/drop traversals, per-node Nat size/div/numeral temporaries replaced by the exact resident index, recursive merge with reallocation): reintroducing any of them is out of scope now. Since the residual cost is allocation/move-bound and the remaining safe micro-choices are measured-neutral, no further candidate has an evidence-based expectation of clearing the 1.03 acceptance gate.

attempts.source_assessment: Measured (instrumented, inflated; wall baseline arbitrary ≈114 µs at n=1024, ≈5.6 µs at n=64): msort 2047 calls (612.6k ns excl.), merge 1023 calls (661.1k ns excl.), less_eq 5120 calls, and one call each per internal node of size_list/gen_length (142k/115k ns), split_at_nat (106k ns), divide_nat (46k ns), nat_of_num_bit0_one/num_bit0/num_one (≈210k/32k/32k ns). The execution equations are already the standard halving merge sort: 2n−1 msort calls, exactly n−1 merges, one owned split per internal node, and each merge level touches all n elements once. Directions considered: (1) bottom-up/pairwise-run merge sort — removes the 2n−1 recursive msort calls, but needs a new sortedness+mset proof for runs composed through msort_sort/properties_for_sort, and in the Vec realization either builds n singleton lists (more allocations) or adds run bookkeeping on top of take/drop, so it does not reduce per-level element work and may worsen allocation; rejected as a large proof for a non-transferable/possibly negative gain. (2) a halving helper `half (x#y#zs) = Suc (half zs)` replacing `size xs div 2` — would cut n Nat-successor additions to n/2 and drop the Nat division, but the computed value is still the length-derived half, and the existing size_list mapping only fixes the value while the guidance already forbids the accumulator artifact and machine shift, so the same saving is available realization-side from the resident container length under the source-derived bound; the marginal gain does not justify re-extraction and retranslation of the only export. (3) a one-pass two-pointer `split_half` removing take/drop and all counting — would realize as interleaved pushes, strictly worse than the existing single owned `split_off` that already fuses take and drop (mapping initial:opportunities:0). (4) `splitAt`/`length` restatements — `splitAt n xs` is the abbreviation of `(take n xs, drop n xs)` and list `size` is `length`, so these are term-identical, not work reductions. (5) buffer-reusing/in-place merge — not expressible as an unchanged HOL list recurrence without altering the exported meaning. Remaining concretely profitable work is realization-level and already guided: derive the split index from the container length with a source-derived bound (no Nat successor loop, no Nat division, no shift), one owned split instead of separate take/drop, merge output with pre-reserved capacity and owned tail append, no Clone/Copy beyond A: Ord. That is the fixed-source Rust stage's scope; no source direction merits a bounded attempt now.

rust-only.stop:
No worthwhile further Rust realization change remains for the CURRENT fixed source. The accepted incumbent (geomean 1.35x, conservative lower 1.32x, no measured regression) already applied every admissible realization improvement, and each remaining measured hotspot is the exact source arithmetic or a mandatory node construction:

1) Exact Nat metadata operations dominate and are irreducible in rust-only. height_eq_plus_two (6912 calls, ~0.61 ms exclusive), node_height (7167, ~0.56 ms), nat_less_eq (7166, ~0.17 ms) and the balL_b/balR_b pairs (3456 each, ~0.44/0.47 ms) all execute the source `ht` reads, the source inclusive `max` comparison, the always-evaluated `ht c + nat_of_num (Bit0 One)` guard, and the `max + one` node height through the registered Nat primitives. The numerals are already folded (Nat::one / the exact value two), stored heights are already borrowed into the additions (no clone-before-add remains), and height_eq_plus_two/height_le/node_height/ht/node_b/balL_b/balR_b/balL/balR/cmp are already #[inline]. Removing any of these additions or the always-evaluated +2 guard, replacing max+1, or substituting a strided/closed-form height or visitation schedule would change the CURRENT source recurrence and is a source-stage change, which this stage forbids.
2) node_b (7167 calls, ~0.80 ms exclusive) performs exactly one allocation per constructed node plus the required node_height computation; identity subtrees are already returned in place (insert EQ returns the original box, delete on Leaf returns the leaf box, delete EQ with a leaf left child returns the right box, split_max base case returns the left box), so no redundant per-level free/reallocate remains. Avoiding the remaining per-node allocation would require mutating an owned node in place (unsafe, forbidden) or interning the two Leaf children of a fresh node (Rc/Arc would change the frozen `Tree` representation).
3) The remaining double discriminant test in insert_b/delete_b (match by reference to pick the cmp route, then move-destructure) is a single discriminant load; the alternative single-destructuring form would force rebuilding the EQ node (an added allocation) and would regress the accepted identity-subtree strategy.

Options considered and rejected as non-improving: dropping `Nat::zero() + two` on the Leaf-right guard path (differs only by a fixed-literal addition that cannot overflow; sub-noise), caching a Nat two (caching across calls, disallowed), and reordering the source max/add sequence (association/operand-order changes not authorized). Since 7167/7166/6912-call metadata sites are the source Nat arithmetic itself and the accepted core allocation count is already one new box per constructed node, no measured work remains that an ownership/inlining/traversal realization change could remove.

rust-only.stop: No worthwhile Rust-only change remains for the CURRENT fixed acomp recurrence. Measured evidence: the accepted accumulator implementation already removed the per-node intermediate list construction/list_append churn (accepted comparison: geomean 10.88x, conservative lower bound 10.73x, no workload regression), so the only remaining hot path is the single depth-first, source-ordered visit in acomp_into (2049 calls = exactly one per AExp node for the largest workload; 2048 constructor emissions + root). That is one match/dispatch, one Box<AExp> deref-and-drop, and one Vec<Instr> push per node, ~10-15 ns/node across descending-64 (1889 ns), duplicates-256 (6881 ns) and descending-1024 (26047 ns); the residual cost is dominated by the mandatory consumption/deallocation of the frozen Box-linked AExp spine plus cache-missing pointer chasing, neither of which can be changed without altering the mapped AExp representation or the fixed source recurrence. The remaining plausible micro-ideas are not admissible or not beneficial: a capacity-sizing prepass would add a full extra traversal (an explicitly permitted metadata pass) but the accepted accumulator's geometric Vec growth is already amortized, and the most recent measured refinement attempt regressed (geomean 0.914x, conservative lower bound 0.857x, up to ~18% slower on descending-1024), matching the pattern that any added per-node work costs more than it saves at these node counts. Instruction emission must stay a1-subtree, then a2-subtree, then exactly one ADD, one instruction constructor per node, with no fusion, reordering, skipping, closed form, or memoization, and Instr/Int/AExp payload representations are frozen (Int non-Copy arbitrary precision, Box-ed Plus), so there is no remaining ownership/allocation/traversal-realization transformation that preserves the CURRENT equations while reducing measured work. Private-helper renaming/removal and inlining hints would be at best no-ops after LLVM inlining of instr_loadi/instr_load/instr_add (their instrumented exclusive times are instrumentation artifacts of non-inlined diagnostic builds). Hence finishing preserves the best measured candidate rather than risking a regression against the 1.03 geomean / no-regression >5% admission rule.

proposal.source_assessment: {"measured_hotspot": "In the instrumented run for descending-1024, src/lib.rs:35:list_append is called 2048 times (1024 Plus nodes x 2 appends) and acomp itself is inclusive-dominant (1.16e9 ns instrumented of a 0.44 s run). The uninstrumented baseline is ~600 us (arbitrary) / ~625 us (checked) for descending-1024, growing superlinearly from 64/256.", "proof_route": "Structural induction on the expression with the accumulator generalized: acomp_acc a acc = acc @ acomp a (base cases by refl, Plus case by the two inductive hypotheses plus associativity of @, i.e. append_assoc); then acomp_acc a [] = acomp a by the Nil/append identity. Final export obligation: unfold i2r_entry_0_def, extensionality, rewrite with the nil lemma.", "proposed_change": "Introduce one private source helper that carries an accumulator (the already-emitted prefix) and never concatenates two non-singleton lists: acomp_acc (N n) acc = acc @ [LOADI n]; acomp_acc (V x) acc = acc @ [LOAD x]; acomp_acc (Plus a1 a2) acc = acomp_acc a2 (acomp_acc a1 acc) @ [ADD]; and define the export as acomp = (lambda a. acomp_acc a []). Semantics and emission order are unchanged (a1's code, then a2's code, then exactly one ADD); only the association/direction of construction changes, which is exactly the source recurrence, so this is a genuine source algorithm change, not a Rust-only tweak.", "realization_plan": "Post-extraction Rust keeps the frozen pub fn acomp(expr: AExp) -> List<Instr> signature and the frozen AExp/Instr/List/Int representations. The private helper takes the accumulator by value and returns it (let mut acc; acc.push(instr); acc), so list_append(acc, [instr]) is one push and the Plus case threads a single owned buffer through both children and the trailing ADD. No Clone bounds are added, Int payloads are still moved once, no numeric operation is introduced, and the existing list_append/mapping entries remain valid for their own equations but are no longer exercised on large operands.", "risks": "Only syntactic/proof-shape risks (constructor qualification, induction hypothesis naming, extensionality step); the mathematical identity is elementary. Instruction order and multiplicity are provably identical, so frozen observations cannot distinguish the results.", "root_cause": "The exported equation acomp (Plus a1 a2) = (acomp a1 @ acomp a2) @ [ADD] builds the result bottom-up: every Plus node concatenates already-materialized sublists, so every instruction of a subtree is moved/recopied once per ancestor. With the Vec realization of List.append (out = xs; out.extend(ys)) this is quadratic element movement plus one or two fresh/reallocated buffers per Plus node, for left- and right-leaning trees alike.", "work_reduction": "Each AST node performs exactly one append-into-accumulator of a singleton list; no non-singleton list is ever appended and no prefix is rebuilt. Under the existing Vec realization that singleton append is a push into the owned accumulator, so total instruction emission is Theta(n) amortized pushes with a single growing buffer, versus Theta(n^2) moved elements and repeated reallocation today. Recursive call count per node is unchanged (3 total calls per Plus), the win is in repeated copying/concatenation work."}
proposal.definitions:
fun acomp_acc :: "aexp \<Rightarrow> instr list \<Rightarrow> instr list" where
  "acomp_acc (N n) acc = acc @ [LOADI n]" |
  "acomp_acc (V x) acc = acc @ [LOAD x]" |
  "acomp_acc (Plus a1 a2) acc = acomp_acc a2 (acomp_acc a1 acc) @ [ADD]"

lemma acomp_acc_append: "acomp_acc a acc = acc @ acomp a"
  by (induction a arbitrary: acc) (auto simp: append_assoc)

lemma acomp_acc_nil: "acomp_acc a [] = acomp a"
  by (simp add: acomp_acc_append)

by (rule ext) (simp add: acomp_acc_nil)

previous_proposal.source_assessment: Measured hotspot: mark_out_aux (220.6ms of 221.1ms total; 564 calls, 1.231M per-element Nat countdown steps, each with one_nat()+minus_nat+zero_nat, and each step a tail rescan). Concrete source reduction (flag-preserving, so no number-theoretic re-proof is needed): mark_out n only ever writes False at positions i >= n (it marks numbers divisible by Suc n, the first being 2*(Suc n)); hence mark_out n bs = bs whenever length bs <= n, and then the whole remaining sieve is the identity: length bs <= n ==> sieve n bs = bs. A revised sieve with that O(1) guard therefore performs strictly fewer marking steps (at upper bound 4096 it drops the ~255 mark_out calls for p > 4095/2, i.e. ~22% of the 1.16M marking steps and of the ~1.23M Nat decrements/one_nat constructions), never changes a single flag (guarded branch returns the untouched list), and additionally lets the later Rust realization exit the scanning loop with an index test instead of a per-element Nat countdown. Proof route (short, no new imports, only existing simp rules mark_out_code, mark_out_aux_simps, length_mark_out): (1) mark_out_aux n m bs = bs when length bs <= m, by list induction with invariant m = Suc m' and length bs' <= m'; (2) mark_out n bs = bs when length bs <= n via mark_out_code; (3) sieve n bs = bs when length bs <= n by list induction; (4) sieve_fast (same three equations plus the guard) equals sieve by list induction, using (2),(3) in the guarded case and the IH in the stepping case. Realization plan: sieve_fast keeps the owned Vec<bool> in place and the guard is one usize/length comparison, so no new bounds or clones; primitives (nat addition/subtraction, bool, list constructors, enumerate/replicate/map_filter) are unchanged. No benchmark-specific case: the guard applies to the whole source-defined family (every n and bs, truncating n=0/1 cases included).
previous_proposal.definitions:
lemma mark_out_aux_noop: "length bs <= m ==> mark_out_aux n m bs = bs"
proof (induct bs arbitrary: m)
  case Nil then show ?case by simp
next
  case (Cons b bs)
  have nz: "m ~= 0" using Cons.prems by (cases m) simp_all
  then obtain m' where m: "m = Suc m'" by (cases m) auto
  have le: "length bs <= m'" using Cons.prems m by simp
  with Cons.hyps have ih: "mark_out_aux n m' bs = bs" .

  "sieve_opt n bs =

lemma sieve_id:
  "length bs ≤ n ⟹ Eratosthenes.sieve n bs = bs"
proof (induct bs arbitrary: n)
  case Nil then show ?case by simp

  case (Cons b bs)
  have h: "length bs ≤ n" using Cons.prems by simp
  show ?case
  proof (cases b)
    case False
    have "Eratosthenes.sieve n (False # bs) = False # Eratosthenes.sieve (Suc n) bs" by simp
    also have "… = False # bs" using Cons.hyps[of "Suc n"] h by simp

rust-only.stop: The accepted incumbent (measured geomean 1.29x over the parent, all three workloads non-regressing) already realizes the fixed source recurrence with the minimal legal work: private `horner_sum_int` reads the stored coefficient slice in place (no `coeffs` Vec clone, no per-iteration `Int` clones, in-place accumulator), visiting coefficients last-to-first with exactly one exact `i2r_numeric::Int` multiplication followed by one exact addition per coefficient. Current instrumentation attributes essentially the entire kernel time to that single loop (src/lib.rs:172 `horner_sum_int` 11375 ns inclusive inside src/lib.rs:189 `poly_entry` 11500 ns inclusive); every other catalogued function is effectively free, and `poly_entry` is invoked once per kernel call, so remaining call/ABI or iterator-adapter overhead is a fixed few nanoseconds rather than a scaling cost. The residual cost is the serial big-integer accumulator chain (`acc *= x; acc += c`), which cannot be parallelized or reassociated and whose operands/events are fixed by the CURRENT equations. Every further reduction I considered changes the source business computation rather than its Rust realization: dropping the multiplication by the initial algebraic zero, branching on evaluation point 0/±1, striding/skipping countdown positions, exponentiation or any closed form all alter the source primitive-event sequence/visitation and would need a proved Isabelle source transformation plus re-extraction, which this frozen-source rust_refinement stage does not permit (source_recurrence_change_allowed=false). Representation/ownership alternatives are also exhausted or barred: the private `Poly` field layout, public signatures (`poly`, `coeffs`, `horner_sum`, `foldr`, `poly_entry`), generic `CommSemiring0` bounds and the frozen `Int` numeric contract (no Copy, no u128/i128, no backend access) are fixed, and an earlier attempt that altered the private `Poly` representation was correctly rejected. A pure `#[inline]` codegen hint is not a worthwhile next change: it would save at most a single call boundary per kernel invocation (well under the 1.03 geomean acceptance rule), so proposing it would consume a candidate without plausible measured benefit. No further Rust-only change with a realistic measured gain remains.

previous_proposal.source_assessment: Measured diagnostic hotspot: foldr (1024 calls, ~367.5 µs inclusive) dominates poly_entry; times/plus each called 1024 times, id 1024 times. Source reduction: add general concrete-Int fast paths for the algebraic special scalars x = 1 and x = -1, with the original Horner evaluation as fallback. For x = 1, evaluation is the right-associated coefficient sum, so the 1024 multiplications and id invocations disappear while suffix-sum order and checked-overflow behavior are unchanged (multiplication by 1 never overflows). For x = -1, evaluation is the alternating right-associated sum using unary negation instead of multiplication by -1; checked negation and multiplication by -1 have the same overflow boundary. All coefficients and all Int inputs are covered; the point-2 workload uses the unchanged fallback. Proof route: list induction proves the two foldr identities, then case analysis on x = 1 / x = -1 proves poly_entry_opt = poly_entry. Realization plan: Rust poly_entry branches on x == 1 and x == -1, implementing coeff_sum/coeff_alt_sum as right-to-left loops directly over the private coefficient slice, avoiding the baseline coeffs clone; the fallback remains Horner. This preserves the revised source recurrence and checked intermediate order.
previous_proposal.definitions:
primrec coeff_sum :: "int list ⇒ int" where
  "coeff_sum [] = 0"
| "coeff_sum (c # cs) = c + coeff_sum cs"

primrec coeff_alt_sum :: "int list ⇒ int" where
  "coeff_alt_sum [] = 0"
| "coeff_alt_sum (c # cs) = c + (- coeff_alt_sum cs)"

lemma foldr_one:
  "foldr (λc b. c + 1 * b) xs 0 = coeff_sum xs"
  by (induction xs rule: list.induct) (simp_all add: coeff_sum.simps)

lemma foldr_minus1:
  "foldr (λc b. c + (-1) * b) xs 0 = coeff_alt_sum xs"
  by (induction xs rule: list.induct) (simp_all add: coeff_alt_sum.simps)

lemma poly_at_1: "poly p (1::int) = coeff_sum (coeffs p)"
  by (simp add: Polynomial.poly_def Groups_List.comm_semiring_0_class.horner_sum_foldr foldr_one)

lemma poly_at_minus1: "poly p (-1::int) = coeff_alt_sum (coeffs p)"
  by (simp add: Polynomial.poly_def Groups_List.comm_semiring_0_class.horner_sum_foldr foldr_minus1)

definition poly_entry_opt :: "int poly ⇒ int ⇒ int" where
  "poly_entry_opt p x =
     (if x = 1 then coeff_sum (coeffs p)
      else if x = -1 then coeff_alt_sum (coeffs p)
      else poly p x)"

lemma poly_entry_opt_correct: "poly_entry_opt p x = poly_entry p x"
  unfolding poly_entry_opt_def Poly_Entry.poly_entry_def
  by (cases "x = 1") (auto simp add: poly_at_1 poly_at_minus1)

Frozen signature pub fn poly_entry(p: &Poly<Int>, x: &Int) -> Int is unchanged and all integer arithmetic stays i2r_numeric::Int addition/subtraction/negation. proposal.source_assessment: {"measured_hotspot": "Diagnostic profile: src/lib.rs:32:gen_fib has 1 call and 60833 ns inclusive; one_nat has 360 calls/8895 ns, zero_nat 181 calls/5314 ns, plus_nat 179 calls/5050 ns on the n-180 workload.", "proof_route": "Induct on the original Fib.gen_fib induction rule to prove fib_iter a b n = Fib.gen_fib a b n. The three source cases are immediate by unfolding fib_iter and Fib.gen_fib: the zero case returns a, the Suc 0 case returns b, and the Suc (Suc n) case uses the induction hypothesis on the recursive call. Then combine that equality with the existing lemma Fib.fib_conv_gen_fib: fib n = gen_fib 0 1 n.", "realization_plan": "Realize fib_iter as a tail-recursive loop: if n is zero return a; otherwise compute next_b = a + b exactly with the paired Nat addition primitive, set a = b, b = next_b, and decrement n by one. The successor branch guarantees the decrement is exact. Hoist the Nat one value outside the loop if predecessor realization needs it. The Fib.fib wrapper becomes fib_iter 0 1 n. No closed form, memoization, benchmark table, numeric narrowing, or new generic bounds are introduced.", "source_ids": ["constant:Fib.fib", "constant:Fib.gen_fib", "constant:Nat.one_nat_inst.one_nat", "constant:Nat.zero_nat_inst.zero_nat", "constant:Nat.plus_nat_inst.plus_nat"], "work_reduction": "The existing gen_fib recurrence tests both n = 0 and n = 1 on every loop iteration and constructs the one instance repeatedly. The proposed private helper fib_iter a b 0 = a and fib_iter a b (Suc n) = fib_iter b (a + b) n is extensionally equal to gen_fib but has only one base case and one successor test per step. For Fib.fib it gives the exact wrapper Fib.fib n = fib_iter 0 1 n. This eliminates the n = 1 comparison and the associated repeated one_nat construction while preserving the exact plus_nat recurrence, zero/one arguments, and all natural-number semantics. It is a general recurrence change for all n, not a benchmark-specific branch."}
proposal.definitions:
fun fib_iter :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "fib_iter a b 0 = a"
| "fib_iter a b (Suc n) = fib_iter b (a + b) n"

lemma fib_iter_gen_fib: "fib_iter a b n = Fib.gen_fib a b n"
  by (induct a b n rule: Fib.gen_fib.induct) (simp_all add: fib_iter.simps)

lemma fib_iter_fib: "Fib.fib n = fib_iter 0 1 n"
  by (simp add: Fib.fib_conv_gen_fib fib_iter_gen_fib)

previous_proposal.reason: Measured profile points at node (667 ns exclusive of 709 ns inclusive) and merge (417 ns exclusive, 1501 ns inclusive) as the dominant costs of the translated program, while the pure numeric primitives cost tens of nanoseconds. This candidate keeps the source equations, recursion route, branch selection and Nat arithmetic identical, and only changes ownership of the list-spine boxes: node_boxed moves the child boxes into the result, and merge moves the selected right-spine subtree out of its box (mem::replace with a Leaf placeholder) and writes the recursive result back into the same box. It also avoids materializing the owned copy of the rank that the source rank increment never consumes, while still performing both rank lookups and the exact mathematical comparison.
previous_proposal.evidence: Diagnostic function instrumentation of the incumbent: merge 2 calls / 1501 ns inclusive / 417 ns exclusive, node 1 call / 709 ns inclusive / 667 ns exclusive, ord_class_less_eq 333 ns inclusive, plus_nat_inst_plus_nat 42 ns, nat_le 41 ns, mht 0 ns. full.stop: No worthwhile semantics-preserving Rust realization change remains, and the measured noise floor exceeds any remaining lever. (1) The accepted incumbent already took the only allocation lever available under the fixed equations: every spine step now reuses the Box that held the source-selected descent subtree (merge_into with mem::replace) and builds the source-selected node from the two already-owned child Boxes (node_boxed), so a spine step performs no malloc/free pair. The profile catalog shows merge_into/node_boxed called with no allocation-helper hotspots left, and the accepted comparison measured 1.369x geomean (conservative lower 1.240), with all three workloads improved (1.41x / 1.38x / 1.32x). (2) The remaining per-spine work is exactly what the CURRENT equation requires: two stored-rank reads (mht l, mht r), one `a1 <= a2` ordering comparison, one exact Nat `+ 1` on the source-selected rank, one source-selected Node, and one recursive merge on the source-selected right subtree -- in that order. Removing anymore (e.g. skipping the +1 when a rank read is zero, or replacing the comparison with a Leaf/zero case analysis) would be a new algebraic case distinction introduced in Rust, not by a checked source transformation, which the fixed-source contract forbids. (3) The residual profile entries (node_boxed 459 ns exclusive, ord_class_less_eq 167, less_eq 292, nat_le 83) come from diagnostic instrumentation that also perturbs inlining of these small #[inline] functions; they are not evidence of removable business work. (4) Empirically the remaining measurements are noise-dominated: for the same parent binary, independent-process medians on descending-64 ranged 32.6-44.9 ns (a ~38% spread), while the whole merge on descending-64 is ~33 ns, i.e. a few nanoseconds per spine node. A previous restructuring attempt measured 0.776x geomean (0.76x / 0.84x / 0.73x), confirming that further reshaping of this hot path costs more than it saves. Returning a further candidate therefore risks replacing an accepted 1.37x improvement with a noise-driven regression rather than reducing kernel runtime.

previous_proposal.reason: Re-submission of the allocation-reuse realisation with the mapping defect fixed: the `constant:Leftist_Heap_Test.node` mapping now names exactly one existing fully qualified item (`crate::node`) instead of the ambiguous `crate::node (private helper: crate::node_boxed_left)` string; the private helper is described only in the `rust` text and in the strategy entries. The Rust content is unchanged from the candidate whose only reported defect was that mapping string: `pub fn node` keeps its signature and delegates to the private `node_boxed_left`, and `merge` uses that helper so the source-selected left child stays in the `Box` the match already owns. Source equations are untouched: Leaf cases return the other argument; the two-node case still compares `a1 <= a2` through `ord_class_less_eq`, still recurses exactly once on the source-selected right subtree with the other node rebuilt from its own boxes, and still runs the source `node` transition in the order `rl = mht l`, `rr = mht r`, `rr <= rl`, one exact Nat plus-one, then the source-selected `Node`. Only representation/ownership changes: one heap allocation and one deallocation per two-node spine step are removed, and small pure helpers are `#[inline]`.
previous_proposal.evidence: Diagnostic instrumentation (baseline, optimization-off, status `measured`): `merge` 2 calls / 2834 ns inclusive / 1000 ns exclusive; `node` 1 call / 1000 ns inclusive / 833 ns exclusive; `ord_class_less_eq` 792/334; `less_eq` 458/416; `nat_le` 84 ns (2 calls); `mht` 83 ns (2 calls); `plus_nat_inst_plus_nat` 42 ns (1 call). Rank arithmetic and rank reads are therefore a few tens of ns, while `merge`/`node` exclusive time dominates, consistent with per-step ownership traffic: the previous bodies moved `*l1` out of its `Box` and `node` immediately allocated a fresh `Box` for that same subtree, so each two-node step paid two allocations plus two deallocations (selected left child and the recursed child box). `node_boxed_left` reuses the pattern-owned child box, leaving one allocation and one deallocation per step, and `#[inline]` on the leaf/rank/comparison helpers removes call overhead at the harness call sites. `mht` still performs exactly one stored-rank read and clone per call, and the rank increment still uses the registered exact Nat-addition primitive with unchanged arbitrary/checked semantics, so no numeric obligation is relaxed and no business transition is added, removed or reordered. Per the stated instrumentation limits these timings are not production allocations counts; the argument rests on the counted allocation/deallocation operations visible in the previous body, not on absolute nanoseconds.

code.explanation:
This error occurs because you tried to mutably borrow a non-mutable variable.

Erroneous code example:

```compile_fail,E0596
let x = 1;
let y = &mut x; // error: cannot borrow mutably
```

In here, `x` isn't mutable, so when we try to mutably borrow it in `y`, it
fails. To fix this error, you need to make `x` mutable:

```
let mut x = 1;
let y = &mut x; // ok!
```
